analysis.title: "The Biggest Opening Bid We Have Ever Recorded In NVDA": Retail Greets Jensen's Exit By Buying 41x More Nvidia Than Normal
key_insights: Nvidia announced that co-founder and only CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately. The stock opened down about 12% on Nov 12, 2026 at around $159, the lowest price since summer 2025, then recovered roughly half of the drop by mid-morning.

Vanda Research (Viraj Patel) reports retail net buying of $111M in the first 30 minutes of trading, 41x a normal open. The median NVDA open sees $2.7M of net retail buying and the 99th percentile is $49M, from 2,480 sessions of opening data since January 2017.

The $111M open beats the prior records of $107M (Feb 26) and $102M (after last August's earnings). Tuesday's $93M open ranks fourth, so two of the four largest retail NVDA opens ever came in the past three sessions.
The $111M net figure came on $799M of gross retail turnover, implying about $455M bought and $345M sold in 30 minutes. Retail sold roughly $3 for every $4 it bought at the open.

Vanda says opens of this size have historically converted into full days of 4-7x, implying $450-770M of retail net buying by the close. That would rank among the top 10 days of retail net buying in any US stock or ETF since 2014. The DeepSeek crash day in January 2025 saw a then-record $562M.

NVDA was the most bought US security on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, at 9.7x, 14.4x and 3.7x the next name. The three-day total through Wednesday is $1.31B, the sixth-highest in 3,735 sessions since 2012, and 61% of all retail net buying across US stocks and ETFs this week.

Retail put $42.5M into the six long 2x NVDA ETFs from Monday to Wednesday, the fifth-largest three-day inflow on record and a 99.8th percentile reading. Inverse NVDA funds saw no net buying despite very strong turnover.

Goldman flagged record leveraged ETF inflows earlier in the week, during the worst week for the S&P since April 2025. Two weeks ago retail was buying the dip while hedging, with a fifth of leveraged ETF flows going to bearish products.

NVDA is down about 15% in five days. The $1.3B of retail buying is about 0.03% of a market cap that exceeded $4T on Friday. Institutions are the likely sellers, with three downgrades and five price target cuts overnight.

Valuation case for dip-buyers: NVDA trades at about 12x forward earnings, the lowest since November 2012 per Reuters, and is the most oversold since 2019. Counterpoint: DeepSeek buyers sat through another 20% drop into April 2025 lows, and after February's record dip buying retail sold the bounce a month later.

Upcoming catalysts: Semafor reports multiple DOJ probes could reach Nvidia, including an antitrust probe of the company. Other items are Huang's possible congressional testimony, a CEO search with no candidate, and Q3 earnings on Tuesday under an interim chief who is also the CFO. The author expects institutions to use retail bids as exit liquidity, and notes retail's morning enthusiasm has tended to turn into afternoon selling this fall.

market_movers.rationale: CEO resignation, DOJ probes, CEO search and Tuesday's earnings under an interim CEO/CFO are open risks. The author sees retail buying as exit liquidity for institutions, while 12x forward earnings gives a valuation case for dip-buyers.

earnings_insights: Nvidia Q3 earnings are due Tuesday (Nov 17, 2026), to be delivered by an interim chief who is also the CFO. No estimates are given in the report.
risk_factors: Further Justice Department probes, including antitrust, could reach Nvidia.
Permanent CEO search with no candidate named.
Q3 earnings on Tuesday delivered by an interim CEO who is also the CFO.
Retail dip buying has historically marked few lows. The DeepSeek buyers saw another 20% drop into April 2025, and retail sold the bounce a month after the February record.
Institutional selling is expected to continue until a buyer other than retail steps up.
vol_and_positioning: Retail flow is one-way long: $111M net buying at the Nov 12 open, $1.31B over three days (61% of all retail net buying in US stocks and ETFs), and $42.5M into long 2x NVDA ETFs (99.8th percentile). Inverse NVDA funds saw no net buying despite strong turnover, so retail has stopped paying for protection.

Vanda expects $450-770M of retail net buying in NVDA on Nov 12, based on the historical 4-7x conversion of large opens. The author expects retail buying to turn into selling in the afternoon, as it has tended to this fall.
geopolitical: Nvidia's CEO resigned over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, per the article. Semafor reports multiple Justice Department probes could sweep up Nvidia, including an antitrust probe aimed at the company.
cross_bank_references: Goldman flagged record inflows into leveraged ETFs during the worst week for the S&P since April 2025, with NVDL among the beneficiaries.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail set a record opening bid of $111M. NVDA trades at about 12x forward earnings, the lowest since 2012, and is the most oversold since 2019. DeepSeek dip buyers were eventually paid, and Vanda expects $450-770M of retail buying on the day.
tension_points.bear_case: Retail buying is about 0.03% of market cap and cannot set the price. Gross turnover shows $3 sold per $4 bought. DeepSeek buyers sat through another 20% drop. Record retail buying rarely marks the low. DOJ probes, the CEO search and earnings under an interim CEO are still ahead, and institutions are likely selling into the bid.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tuesday's third-quarter earnings under the interim CEO/CFO, and whether the $160 level holds.

theme_stances.key_argument: Retail can set records but not the price, and institutions are likely using the record bid as exit liquidity.
theme_stances.evidence: the smart money is using the biggest retail bid in Nvidia's history as exit liquidity
